newsitem.title: USA: CFTC prods CBOT on wheat contract changes.
newsitem.headline: CFTC prods CBOT on wheat contract changes.

text.p: Commodity Futures Trading Commission Chairwoman Brooksley Born said Monday that the Chicago Board of Trade told the agency it was not able to yet come up with a recommendation for changing the delivery terms of its wheat contract, as requested by the CFTC.
"I am considering putting this out for public comment," Born told reporters after addressing the Millers National Federation annual meeting.
Born said she would decide on whether to seek public comment on the controversial issue within two weeks.
"I am certainly concerned that the CBOT has not been able to come up with a proposal," Born said. "They haven't given us any sense of where they are going or how long it will take."
Born said the CBOT last week notified the agency that it was unable to reach a recommendation for delivery changes in the 120-day period given to it by the CFTC.
Born also said that the CFTC had received more than 300 comments from the public about a similar issue related to the CBOT and its corn and soybean contracts.
The agency has pressed CBOT to make changes to its corn and soybean contracts to reflect changes in storage facilities and to prevent market manipulation.

When asked how soon the CFTC would take final action on the corn and soybean contract changes, Born declined to give a specific time frame. She said only that the agency hoped to "focus on all the issues" after mid-June, when an extension of the public comment period ends.

The changes in delivery terms for the CBOT's corn and soybean contracts has emerged as one of the most contentious issues before the CFTC is recent years. Scores of farmers, grain cooperatives and politicians have told the CFTC they oppose the CBOT's proposed changes.
